surprises: The FY2011 tax rate goes UP (14.20 to 16.16) while total valuation goes DOWN ($1,227m to $1,114m) — the levy still rises 3.3%. The valuation and tax history table on p12 shows this plainly and is the only place in the report it is visible.

The New Growth Revenue table on p12 uses a DIFFERENT tax rate for the same fiscal year than the valuation table immediately above it — FY2011 new growth is priced at 14.20 while the FY2011 rate is 16.16. It appears to apply the prior year's rate. Joining the two tables on fiscal year would silently mix rates.

This is the year the town STOPPED printing vital statistics in detail. The p80 note says so explicitly, citing the Registry of Vital Records and the US Department of State. Any name-level series ends here.

The Housing Partnership roster on p7 carries rows reading '2009 3 Vacancies / 2008 5 Vacancies / 2007 5 Vacancies' — unfilled seats recorded going back three years, in a table that otherwise lists people.

Monty Tech reports vocational programme enrollment WITH a gender split for every one of its twenty programmes (p49-52): Dental Assisting 3 male / 55 female, Electrical 78 male / 6 female, Business Technology 11 male / 49 female. Nothing else in this report breaks any population down by sex.

Charter and school choice tuitions both missed their appropriations badly in opposite directions (p65): Choice Tuitions spent $355,494 against $284,958 appropriated; Charter Tuitions spent $259,434 against $325,360. The two errors nearly cancel in the total.

The p13 burial list has about 22 entries; the p80 vitals report says 58 deaths. The two are counting different things (burials in town cemeteries vs. deaths recorded by the clerk) and nothing on either page says so.
recovered: The correction turns this document from a mostly-narrative report into a mostly-tabular one. What is legible now and was not: every one of the six directory tables at the front (office hours, meeting schedule, elected officials, appointed officials, the town-at-a-glance block), which now read as clean label/value pairs instead of a wall of names; all five school staff rosters, with room numbers, house colours and grade sections intact; the Turkey Hill MCAS table on p41, which is a complete four-column grid and was not recorded in the previous inventory at all; the FY2011 receipts detail on p58, where two of three column pairs are now perfectly clean including every state aid line; the general fund expenditure ledger from p62 to p65 including its GRAND TOTAL row; the special revenue funds list across pp66-70 with its GRAND TOTAL; the capital project funds table on p71; the treasurer's cash reconciliation on p72, which ties to its own printed total; the FY2012 omnibus budget on pp84-85 with all its subtotals and the TOTAL OMNIBUS BUDGET; and the Article 19 capital plan on p83, which is the complete version of a table that is still wrecked where it first appears on pp13-14. Monty Tech's per-programme enrollment with gender splits (pp49-52) is now recoverable by regex and was invisible before. What is still NOT legible: pages 60-61, which remain split into a page of labels and a page of values and are the exact failure the correction was supposed to fix — the whole GENERAL GOVERNMENT section of the expenditure ledger cannot be re-paired without geometry. The trust funds (pp73-74), the debt repayment schedule (pp76-77), the collection of taxes (p78) and the town election results (pp79-80) are all still printed 180 degrees out, with headers at the bottom of the page and row labels displaced from their values; the tax collection page has no row labels at all. Page 97, the first page of the payroll report, is entirely empty in the OCR. The combined balance sheet on p56 is missing its heading and its entire asset section above the tax receivables, and its six money columns have no headers. The SUMMARY OF RECEIPTS on p58 has all ten of its labels and none of its values, including the GRAND TOTAL that would let the receipts detail be reconciled. Both pie charts (pp57, 59) are missing their largest slices. The Nashoba health counts (pp18-20) lose numbers into their dot leaders, and every communicable disease count on p20 is gone.
